name: Alopecia Totalis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Alopecia Totalis

criteria.description: Complete loss of scalp hair without scarring
Absence of clinical or histological signs of scarring alopecia
Identification of exclamation mark hairs at the periphery of bald patches
Negative fungal culture to exclude tinea capitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Complete scalp hair loss without scarring plus exclusion of other causes such as scarring alopecia or fungal infection
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; biopsy may be used to exclude other causes.

laboratory: Possible elevated thyroid antibodies in some cases
genetic: Association with HLA class II alleles (e.g., HLA-DRB1*1104)
Polymorphisms in immune regulatory genes (e.g., CTLA4, PTPN22)
other: Trichoscopy showing exclamation mark hairs and yellow dots
Scalp biopsy demonstrating peribulbar lymphocytic infiltrate ('swarm of bees' pattern)

distinguishingFeatures: Patchy rather than total scalp hair loss
Inflammatory signs and follicular dropout on biopsy
Scaling and broken hairs with black dots

redFlags: Rapid progression of hair loss with scalp ulceration
Signs of secondary infection (e.g., pustules, fever)
Presence of scarring or atrophy on scalp examination
references: Hordinsky MK, Ericson M. Alopecia areata: clinical presentation, diagnosis, and unusual cases. Dermatol Clin. 2013;31(1):1-12.
Messenger AG, McKillop J, Farrant P, McDonagh AJG, Sladden M. British Association of Dermatologists’ guidelines for the management of alopecia areata 2012. Br J Dermatol. 2012;166(5):916-926.

Strazzulla LC, Wang EHC, Avila L, Lo Sicco K, Brinster N, Christiano AM, et al. Alopecia areata: An appraisal of new treatment approaches and overview of current therapies. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018;78(1):15-24.
